title: January reopening readiness: a first-week checklist
description: A practical checklist for Kenyan school principals on making sure the school is truly ready for reopening, so the first week of the new year runs smoothly.
body:
The first week back sets the tone for the whole year. A school that has prepared opens calmly and gets straight to teaching. One that has not spends the week fixing problems that could have been solved in the holiday.

Use this checklist about two weeks before reopening, and again a few days before.

Before anyone returns

Facilities and systems

  • Classrooms, dormitories, toilets, and kitchens cleaned and inspected
  • Water and electricity tested, and any repairs done
  • Furniture counted and placed, with spare desks and beds identified
  • Security arrangements and emergency contacts confirmed
  • First aid supplies stocked

Academic readiness

  • Timetable published and checked for clashes
  • Class lists and pathway assignments confirmed, including new Grade 10 learners
  • Teaching staff allocations confirmed, and gaps covered
  • Schemes of work and teaching materials ready

People and communication

Staff and parents

  • Staff return dates communicated and a briefing meeting planned
  • Parents sent reporting dates, fee details, and requirements
  • New staff and new learners given an orientation plan
  • Fee collection systems and payment channels tested

Walk the school yourself: A short walk through the compound in the last week of the holiday, with a checklist in hand, will find problems that reports do not. Take the bursar and the deputy with you.

The first week itself

Keep the first days simple. Welcome students, explain routines and expectations, settle new learners, and begin teaching early. Resist the urge to schedule heavy events in the first few days. Take attendance from day one, and follow up quickly on any learner who has not reported.
